heading: Float (`FLOAT_LIT`)
text:
### Float (`FLOAT_LIT`) [LLEX.11.2]

```
FLOAT_LIT ::= DEC_LIT '.' DEC_LIT EXPONENT?
           |  DEC_LIT EXPONENT
EXPONENT  ::= ('e' | 'E') ('+' | '-')? DIGIT ('_'? DIGIT)*
```

idris.name: llex_11_2__accepted_spellings
idris.note: Seven `FLOAT_LIT` spellings read to their decimals, each `Refl`: `1500.0`, `1.5e3`, `1.5E3`, `1.5e+03`, `15e2`, `1_500.0`, and `1e1_0`, the separator in an exponent the production admits.

idris.name: llex_11_2__dec_more
idris.note: The digits after the first of a `DEC_LIT`, with the value and the count so far: a digit continues the run, a `_` continues it when a digit follows ([LLEX.11.1]'s `('_'? DIGIT)*`) and ends the literal otherwise, any other codepoint ends the run and is handed back.

idris.name: llex_11_2__dec_run
idris.note: A `DEC_LIT` at the head of a text: a digit, then `llex_11_2__dec_more`; its value, its digit count and the text after it; nothing when no digit opens it.

idris.name: llex_11_2__exponent
idris.note: An `EXPONENT` after its marker: an optional sign, then a `DEC_LIT` that ends the text, its signed value; a `_` before a digit is admitted as the production's `DIGIT ('_'? DIGIT)*` places it (`1e1_0` is `1e10`), and [LLEX.12.1.1] says the same: the unit `_` never stands inside a scientific literal, and a `_` within it is a digit-group separator. logical/LCST.4.5.8_separator_in_exponent spells the admitted and the refused placements and agrees with libds under idris-libds.

idris.name: llex_11_2__float_lit
idris.note: A `FLOAT_LIT`, the whole text: `DEC_LIT '.' DEC_LIT EXPONENT?` or `DEC_LIT EXPONENT`, both sides of the point required ([LLEX.11.2.1]) and the exponent required on the bare form ([LLEX.11.2.2]); its value as the digits and the power of ten they sit at.

idris.name: llex_11_2__refused_spellings
idris.note: Nine texts that are no `FLOAT_LIT`, each `Refl`: `1.` and `.5` (one side of the point), `1500` (an `INT_LIT`), `1.5e` (no exponent digits), `1_.5`, `1._5` and `1.5e_1` (a separator beside the point or the marker), `0x1p3` (a hex float, [LLEX.11.2.3]), ` 1.5` (a space).
